subject: Priority burst pool request + feature dependency check
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harper <tom.harper@blueharbor.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority burst pool request + product clarity for BlueHarbor launch

Hi team —

BlueHarbor (Tom cc'd) confirmed their rollout date: 2027-07-20. Their forecast (attached) shows a spike on day-of of ~600 RPS sustained for 30 minutes and a 150–200 RPS 4-hour tail. They asked us for a temporary higher-rate allowance on the day of launch (priority burst pool) plus assurance that two features are on the serving roadmap: 1) prefix KV caching and 2) deduped batching for similar prompt templates.

Quick asks:
- Karthik / Marissa: can we commit to a temporary burst pool (target headroom ~3x current allotment) for 07/20, and what approvals do we need?
- Marcus: what are the infra constraints for enabling a short-lived burst pool (30–60m) at that scale in us-west? Any risks to other tenants?
- Product: do we have a timeline for prefix KV caching and deduped batching, or an acceptable mitigation?

Attached: blueharbor_traffic_model_v1.xlsx (forecast) and feature_dependency_matrix_v2.pdf (high-level ask).

I don't want to surprise the customer — let's try to get a clear yes/no and any guardrails by EOD.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Lead — Growth
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harper <tom.harper@blueharbor.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority burst pool request + product clarity for BlueHarbor launch

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and for looping Monica in on the support side. A couple of notes from the commercial/commitment angle:

- BlueHarbor will sign a one-time surge addendum if we can provide the burst window and rate cap. They prefer a confirmed headroom number.
- Deal team is comfortable with a short-term add-on fee for the burst. Deal id DH-4192-BH.
- Timeline: we need engineering and product sign-off by COB tomorrow to keep procurement timelines sane (legal needs 48h for addendum).

Action items for product/infra + ask for Marcus:
- Confirm whether a 3x headroom is safe and what the exact token/RPS caps should be.
- If we need to route to a fallback model (smaller, quantized variant) under overload, what's the expected quality delta?

I'll coordinate the billing language once we have the capacity confirmation.

Karthik
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Tom Harper <tom.harper@blueharbor.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 12:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority burst pool request + product clarity for BlueHarbor launch

On Mon, Jul 5, 2027 at 10:03 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jordan — thanks for the heads up and for looping Monica in on the support side.

Short version: a temporary 3x headroom for a 30–60 minute window in us-west is feasible with the following caveats and guardrails:

- We need a hard cap and an automatic routing policy that fails over to a smaller quantized model (q4 variant) at 2.5x if latency exceeds 450ms P50. That prevents noisy neighbors.
- Enabling the burst pool requires a manual ops window (30 min lead time) to pre-warm GPU pools and load KV caches. We can script most of this but will require an on-call infra engineer to trigger and monitor.
- Risk: if other customers have concurrent scheduled bursts, capacity contention could cause throttling; recommend setting the window and a UTC timestamp and adding the customer to the temporary 'reserved_burst' list.

Please see notes attached (blueharbor_traffic_model_v1.xlsx referenced) — I mocked a small simulation: 600 RPS for 30m maps to ~3.6M tokens if average prompt+response is 100 tokens. With current pool sizes that hits ~78% GPU utilization on the provisioned fleet during the spike — acceptable if we enforce the failover policy above.

Questions for product: is prefix KV caching ship-ready in the next 2–3 weeks? If not, we need to expect higher token cost during the tail.

Marcus
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer — Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harper <tom.harper@blueharbor.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority burst pool request + product clarity for BlueHarbor launch

Thanks — quick product update following internal dev sync:

- Prefix KV caching: shipping to dedicated fleet in canary this week (internal milestone met). We can enable it for BlueHarbor's dedicated pool as an opt-in; full production roll-out across hosted customers is scheduled for late August.
- Deduped batching for template-heavy prompts: roadmap item with a targeted experimental release in mid-August. No guaranteed timeline for GA.

Given that caching can be applied to a dedicated pool, recommended plan:
1) Approve a temporary reserved burst window on 2027-07-20 for 30 minutes (start time in UTC to be determined).
2) Apply prefix KV caching to BlueHarbor's dedicated pool prior to the window (requires pre-warm).
3) Add the q4 failover routing Marcus suggested as a safety valve.

I'll tag engineering to prepare the opt-in steps. If legal needs a product description for the addendum, I can draft a short paragraph on what caching implies and expected improvements.

Marissa
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harper <tom.harper@blueharbor.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2027 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priority burst pool request + product clarity for BlueHarbor launch

Appreciate the quick turns — summary and next steps:

- Decision: approve one-time reserved burst window on 2027-07-20 for 30 minutes, target 3x headroom relative to their current allotment.
- Guardrails: q4 routing failover at 2.5x if latency P50 > 450ms; infra to pre-warm and monitor; set explicit UTC start time once Tom confirms their deploy plan.
- Product commitments: Marissa will enable prefix KV caching on BlueHarbor's dedicated pool ahead of the window; deduped batching is not guaranteed for this launch. Marissa to provide wording for the legal addendum.
- Commercial: Karthik to prepare one-time surge addendum; Monica to prepare CS runbook (on-call contact, escalation path).

Tom — could you confirm the preferred UTC start time for the window (and whether the 30-minute duration is OK) by EOD tomorrow? Once we have a time we will schedule the pre-warm and provide the formal addendum.

Attachments referenced: blueharbor_traffic_model_v1.xlsx, feature_dependency_matrix_v2.pdf

Thanks all,
Jordan
